notes: Volume M–O of the collection: 79 pages, 56 entries (39 under M, 9 under N, 8 under O) covering architects, builders, developers, an engineer, a landscape architect, a preservationist and three firms, read end to end — the title page, the three letter indexes, every entry (education, firms, cultural identification, narrative and footnotes), every 'Projects in San Francisco' and 'Other notable projects' list, and every figure caption. The fifth of the eight letter-range PDFs; A–C, D–F, G–I and J–L are done. No inventory table and no APN anywhere, so the record-parcel check resolve_eas.py's report prints has nothing to test against. Six entries yielded no numbered San Francisco address: Donald MacDonald's only San Francisco work is the Bay Bridge; Charles McCarthy, Edith Mortensen Northman and Theodore Osmundson have no numbered San Francisco project at all; Rai Okamoto's two are the Japantown redevelopment and the Buchanan Mall; Michael O'Shaughnessy's are tunnels, a reservoir and the Hetch Hetchy system; and William Mooser II's single entry is Ghirardelli Square. The largest single loss is William Gladstone Merchant's list of about thirty recreation centres, playgrounds and field houses, which the volume gives by park name with no street number. Morrow & Morrow has a full entry that the M index does not list, so the index count and the entry count differ.

coverage.note: 417 numbered-address mentions across 79 pages became 247 findings. The gap is the unnumbered and the repeated: about thirty of William Gladstone Merchant's recreation buildings, the Masten & Hurd school and stadium commissions and several tracts are given by park, campus or cross street with no street number, and the rest are addresses printed twice — Frederick Meyer's and Smith O'Brien's entries share five buildings, Gertrude Morrow's and Irving Morrow's share their whole list with the Morrow & Morrow firm entry, and August Nordin's New Era Hall appears in his narrative and again in his project list. 212 of the 247 reached a parcel and 35 did not: 15 numbers the city no longer has, 12 recorded ranges now split across separate parcels, 6 condominiums, 1 address EAS holds that no active parcel does, and 1 given only as One Bush Plaza. Of the 212, 158 were published onto 157 pages (83 created by this run) across 21 neighborhood directories, and 54 were declined: 42 already carried by a survey or statement that documented the building first, 7 on parcels with no 2025 secured-roll row, 3 undated pieces of work with no component to carry them, 1 on a parcel a sibling record already documents, and 1 on the parcel that stands for the whole of Golden Gate Park. 71 pages state a construction-date disagreement with the assessor and 16 state, unadjudicated, a disagreement in the record itself or that the building described may not be the one standing.
